author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing opens on its first page for a page value below 1
summary: A reader requesting the owner listing with a page value below 1 sees the first page instead of the error page. Page values of 1 or above behave as before.
acceptance_criteria: given a page value of 0, -1, or the lowest value the request accepts, when the owner listing is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 with the normal listing showing the first page's owners, not the error page
given a page value below 1, when the owner listing renders, then the first page is shown as the current page in the pagination controls
given a search with a page value below 1, when it runs, then the outcome matches the same search on the first page: one match opens that owner's record, and no match reports that no owner was found
given a page value of 1 or above, when the owner listing is requested, then the requested page is shown as before
non_goals: The veterinarian directory's page handling: the owner's report names 'the owner listing' only; recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md
Page values that are not numbers: the report covers 'any page value below 1'
Page values past the last page: the report covers 'any page value below 1'
The error page's content (REQ-SYS-002 known defect)
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1, which quotes 'treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200)'; its decisions list is empty and no recorded requirement or Non-Goals row conflicts, so no consultation was raised. Reversible decision by the product expert: 'as the first page' keeps the REQ-OWN-002 outcomes, so a single match still opens that owner's record and no match still reports none found, rather than forcing a listing. docs/prd.md carries the new requirement, its acceptance bullets, edge case 4, and an open question on the veterinarian directory. The prd-autofix audit found no records.

risks.risk: Clamping inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, for example Math.max(page - 1, 0), leaves currentPage below 1 in the model, and page - 1 overflows to a large positive index at Integer.MIN_VALUE.

risks.risk: A stub matching any(Pageable.class) answers an overflowed index as readily as page 0, so a test at Integer.MIN_VALUE can pass against a wrong fix.
risks.mitigation: The tests assert the Pageable reaching the repository is page index 0, by capture or an eq stub, and assert the currentPage model attribute is 1 (docs/testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: a stub is a conscious exception and must not hide the behavior).

author: system-design-expert
answer: Finding 1: the requirement stands, the mechanism changes. The page-index pin stays; the captor goes. This narrows design-block line 5 risk 2 from 'by capture or an eq stub' to the eq stub alone. Why the pin stays: the finding's claim that the model pins the page holds only for today's code, where one local feeds both. The test must also fail on a wrong fix. Math.max(page - 1, 0) in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName plus Math.max(page, 1) in addPaginationModel gives currentPage 1 on every row, while page - 1 overflows at Integer.MIN_VALUE to a huge index. An any(Pageable.class) stub still answers that, so nothing but the index catches it. Why the captor goes: docs/testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy, 'A stub is a stand-in, not an assertion', says to assert an argument that is the behavior through the observable outcome, and the test-review checklist flags a captor where a whole expected object can be built. Do this: replace stubTwoOwnersOnAnyPage() with a helper taking the page index, stubbing findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), eq(PageRequest.of(pageIndex, OWNERS_PAGE_SIZE))) to return the two owners. OWNERS_PAGE_SIZE is a named test constant, since the page size is a local in the controller. Below-one callers pass FIRST_PAGE_INDEX, which stays, and the page-2 test passes REQUESTED_PAGE - 1. A wrong index then gets no stubbed page, the unstubbed mock returns null, and the handler fails, so the test goes red through the response with no verify. Delete requestedPageIndex(), the ArgumentCaptor import, and the assertThat import if nothing else uses it. Keep currentPage REQUESTED_PAGE in the page-2 test. So apply finding 1 except its deletion of FIRST_PAGE_INDEX and its loss of the index pin. Finding 2: apply it; the merge is legitimate. docs/prd.md carries one Done-when bullet for this ('its first page is shown as the current page'); the prd-entry's two acceptance criteria split it. docs/testing-principles.md § Coverage says a second test through the same class proves nothing further, and the declared test sends page=0, already a row. The merge also strengthens the test: currentPage 1 then holds at Integer.MIN_VALUE too, which is what risk 2 asks for and the separate page=0 test never showed. Add model().attribute("currentPage", 1) to the parameterized test, delete theOwnerListingShouldMarkTheFirstPageAsCurrentForAPageValueBelowOne, and rename the parameterized test theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageAsCurrentForPageValuesZeroMinusOneAndTheLowestAcceptedValue. coverage-map will then mark both declared names absent; note each with the carrying test's name, per tdd-workflow § completion walk. No gate reads test_names beyond that map. The repository boundary double is unchanged: the existing @MockitoBean framework stub, now argument-bound; this response names that form for the test reviewer.
notes: Not run: I did not execute the eq-stub form or the wrong-fix mutation, because the tree is outside my write scope. The null-then-failure path is read from OwnerController.processFindForm (ownersResults.isEmpty()) and assumes Mockito's default answer for a Page return type; the implementer's Red run confirms it. The @BeforeEach Franklin stub does not interfere, since the listing tests search with an empty last name. The search test at page=0 keeps its any(Pageable.class) stubs: its outcome is the redirect or notFound, and the index pin lives in the listing test. No durable write: docs/testing-principles.md already carries the governing rule.
